text: Em um jogo emocionante da Northbridge League, Seabrook Town venceu o Harbour City por 4 a 2, revirando o placar no segundo tempo. Apesar do excelente desempenho de Marek Barros, que marcou 1 gol e deu 2 assistências, com a melhor nota da partida 9.8 [#975], a expulsão de Joon Whitfield aos 43 minutos deixou Harbour City com um jogador a menos [#871]. Seabrook Town usou seu estilo de jogo aberto, cruzando várias vezes e pressionando mais a partir dos 65 minutos, o que resultou em 3 gols na segunda etapa [#1361]. Nos acréscimos, Kian Romano brilhou, marcando dois gols quase seguidos para garantir a virada, mostrando muita eficiência nas oportunidades que teve, com xG alto de 0.609 e 0.959 (chances boas para gols) [#1882] [#1906]. Harbour City, mesmo com toque paciente e boas chances no primeiro tempo, não resistiu ao ritmo e velocidade da equipe visitante no final.

social: Que virada! Seabrook Town sai atrás, mas vence Harbour City por 4 a 2 com golaços nos minutos finais!
Marek Barros brilhou com gol e 2 assistências, mas a expulsão complicou para o Harbour City.
Kian Romano decidiu com dois gols no fim e garantiu a vitória do Seabrook Town na Northbridge League!

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in pt

- Marek Barros had the highest individual xG in the match with 0.72, scored 1 goal and provided 2 assists with a standout rating of 9.8 [#975].
- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals on 22 shots with an xG of 3.48, demonstrating efficient finishing compared to Harbour City's 2 goals on 10 shots and xG of 1.0.
- The red card to Joon Whitfield at 43' left Harbour City with 10 men early in the second half, likely influencing the shift in momentum [#871].
- Kian Romano scored a late brace at 90+2' and 90+3' with high xG chances of 0.609 and 0.959, sealing the victory for Seabrook Town [#1882, #1906].
- Seabrook Town increased pressing intensity and directness from 65', which preceded their three second-half goals and comeback win [#1361].

- Seabrook Town exploited their wide, crossing play style (3-4-3 formation) to create multiple scoring opportunities, reflected in their higher xG (3.48) and more box touches (57 vs. 42) than Harbour City, indicating effective use of flank overloads and crosses into the box [team_stats], [team_styles].
- Harbour City’s patient short passing approach (4-2-3-1) is evident in their longest goal build-up: a 17-pass sequence lasting 56.7s leading to Elias Okafor’s goal, showcasing methodical ball retention and positional play to break down Seabrook's defense [goals, evidence 904,905].
- The assist types show tactical variety: Marek Barros scored from a long-distance cross following a corner rebound, evidencing Harbour City’s set piece threat within their generally patient style [goal at 47’, assist_type: cross, evidence 975].
- Seabrook’s tactical shift at 65’ to press higher and play more direct—intended to chase the game—increased their press intensity (0.84 from 0.66) and line height (0.72 from 0.60), resulting in quick regains leading to goals shortly after, such as Callum Varga’s through ball finish following a regain [key_moments 1361, goal 69’].
- Kian Romano’s late goals came from quick counters and short combination plays after regains, illustrating Seabrook’s effective counter-attacking prowess enabled by their higher pressing and directness after the tactical change [goal 90+2’ and 90+3’, build_up involves regains, evidence 1881,1882,1905].
- Harbour City’s late tactical change to press higher and adopt more direct play was a response to trailing and aligned with the need to regain territory quickly; however, this intensified pressing exposed them to conceding under direct counters, as evidenced by the goals conceded immediately after [key_moments 1884, last two goals].
